evidence.description: Modification of private state variables inside an asynchronous Task.

candidates.explanation: The `items` set is updated within an asynchronous `Task` block. While the class is marked with `@MainActor`, the `Task` closure captures `self` and modifies `items` and `activeTasks`, which could lead to race conditions if the task is not strictly executed on the main thread or if the internal state management logic is bypassed by concurrent access.
candidates.title: Potential Thread Safety Issue in Asynchronous State Mutation

evidence.description: The download method proceeds to create a new Task without checking if a task for the given URL is already active in the dictionary.

candidates.explanation: The `download` method creates a new `Task` every time it is called, but it does not check if the task is already in progress before adding to the `activeTasks` dictionary, potentially leading to multiple concurrent downloads for the same URL.
candidates.title: Duplicate Concurrent Requests for Same URL

evidence.description: Custom hash and equality implementations only consider the URL property.

candidates.explanation: The `Item` struct implements `Hashable` and `Equatable` based only on the `url` property, but the `data` property is not used in the equality check or hash calculation, which may lead to unexpected behavior if two items with the same URL but different data are compared.
candidates.title: Inconsistent Hashable/Equatable Implementation
